authoringNotes.status: approximate centreline from 2026 OpenStreetMap ways, traced against GSI gazo3 1984–1986 aerials and the 1:25,000 Nara sheet (1983 revision, published 1984-05-30); not surveyed or native-qualified
authoringNotes.sprintRoute: Sanjō-dōri west of the JNR level crossing → JNR Nara Station front → Sanjō-dōri east past Sarusawa-ike and the Kōfuku-ji pagoda → Ichi-no-torii → north past the museum to Kenchō-higashi → Route 369 north → east past Kaidan-in, north beside Daibutsu-ike and the Shōsō-in → Shin-Wakakusayama toll gate → switchbacks via Mikasa Onsen and Jikkoku-dai → Wakakusa-yama summit car park
authoringNotes.topologyReason: A city run into a hill climb with real, distinct endpoints. Sanjō-dōri's station section was eastbound-only and the driveway beyond the summit is a one-way, unpaved forest road, so no legal 1986 loop returns to the start without a fabricated return leg.
authoringNotes.oneWay: Sanjō-dōri 樽井町–国鉄奈良駅前 eastbound only 8:00–21:00 from December 1965 (奈良県公報4473); driven eastbound on a weekday before 21:00. The climb is driven uphill from the north gate, the legal direction whether two-way (today) or one-way north→south (the through course). The one-way unpaved Kasuga Okuyama road beyond the summit is not used.
authoringNotes.designations: Route 369 (designated 1975-04-01) along 登大路 and north from 県庁東, shown in national-road colour on the 1983 map. The Ichi-no-torii–Kenchō-higashi road became Route 169 only on 1993-04-01; show no 169 shield.
authoringNotes.elevationsAndWidths: Elevations from the GSI dem5a laser DEM (modern), smoothed over about ±40 m and limited to 12% per control-point edge; at most about 6 m below the raw DEM near Jikkoku-dai. Half-widths are authored estimates: Sanjō-dōri 3.8–4.4 m (about 8 m wide in 1986), Ichi-no-torii–Route 369 4.6–4.8 m, the Tōdai-ji lane 3.0 m, the driveway 3.3 m. The tightest hairpins were narrowed to 2.7–3.2 m for the curvature bound until they were opened (see hairpins); the driveway is 3.3 m throughout.
authoringNotes.cornerGeometry: Quadratic tangent trims in millimetres, not physical radii. City corners use one control point with 12–18 m trims (compiled radii 8.6–13.4 m). On the driveway a control point is placed on the smoothed OSM centreline after about 28° of heading change or 70 m, never closer than 7.5 m, with the maximum trim. That trace compiled to a tightest radius of 5.8 m, against 5.6 m on the OSM centreline. The Kaidan-in, Daibutsu-ike and Shōsō-in corners now take 17–18 m trims, and fourteen driveway bends are 13 m arcs (see hairpins).
authoringNotes.pacing: One-dimensional model of the handling constants and the test-driver rule (check.ts): 146.5 s. Run read-only against the repo's generated eight-car AI races, the same model was within 1% of the AI winner on irohazaka-1986 (170.6 against 172.4 s) and kyoto-1986 (198.6 against 201.0 s), and 13% fast on aizu-wakamatsu-1986 (129.2 against 148.3 s). Expect an AI winner of about 150–170 s and a last car of about 160–185 s; targetMs 180000 sits at the slow end. Before the hairpins were opened, the AI could not hold its 850 mm/tick floor through the 6–10 m hairpins, and some of them no car could steer at all.
authoringNotes.musicCues: Provisional jo-ha-kyū markers at the modelled arrival times: level crossing start, Ichi-no-torii, toll gate, Mikasa Onsen hairpins, Jikkoku-dai, sky ridge. The asset and digest are placeholders.
authoringNotes.notForProfile: Not in STREET_ROUTE_IDS or the native catalog. This input cannot be submitted to any live profile.
authoringNotes.unconfirmed: 1986 public status and direction of the Tōdai-ji lane (大仏殿北・正倉院西); 1986 paving, width and toll of the climb; the 1986 prefectural number of the Ichi-no-torii–Kenchō-higashi road; whether Sanjō-dōri was under community-road works in 1986.
authoringNotes.hairpins: Opened on 2026-10-29 so that a car can take every bend. The native steering cannot turn a car tighter than about 10.6 m at any speed, and the traced driveway had hairpins of 6.7–9.5 m at the engine’s 5 m cell scale. Fourteen bends from Mikasa Onsen to the summit were redrawn as minimum-radius (Dubins) paths with a 13 m centreline radius, between anchors on each bend’s own legs, and resampled as control points about 5.5 m apart. The Mikasa, S-bend upper and Jikkoku loops keep their bulb shape; the S-bend’s lower loop leaves by a longer exit straight, so the legs stay at least 4 m apart. Gates moved to the nearest new point: mikasa-onsen 11.8 m, hairpin-stack 5.5 m, jikkoku-dai 16.2 m. Grades were eased to at most 12% per edge, changing no elevation by more than 0.9 m. Every bend now allows at least 71 km/h on its widest line at the 5 m cell scale, and the route is 135 m shorter (6.225 km). The original trace is world/research/routes/nara-1986.trace.json.
